messages.subject: Two Servers attending only one client
messages.subject_clean: Two Servers attending only one client
messages.body_plain:
Hello, i am new at simmer and i have the following problem:

Imagine you have a traditional queue problem that has to be modeled with simmer, But this problem has following particularities:
1.- there are two servers and only one queue.
2.- if a client arrive, and both servers are available, then both servers are going to attend the client and reduce service time at the half.
3.- if both server are attending one client and another client arrives to the system, them one server is going to attend the new client,
and the service remaining time for the first client doubles.

here i live attached my code, i have done it but without conditions 2 and 3, just the simple system with 2 servers.
thanks for your comments

This is a good starting point. Now you need to add a mechanism to
update the service time as a function of the number of free servers.
The set_attribute activity would be useful to save the service start
time, a multiplier (number of free servers + 1) and the service time
after applying this multiplier (delay for one server / multiplier).
Finally, you need some signaling (see ?trap and ?send) to update the
latter when an arrival releases the resource or a new arrival enters
the server.

Iñaki

Then I would use auxiliary resources as token buckets. E.g. (not tested):

main <- trajectory() %>%
  seize("resource") %>%
  timeout(service) %>%
  release("resource") %>%
  select(paste0("type", 1:3), "round-robin") %>%
  set_capacity_selected(1)

type1 <- trajectory() %>%
  seize("type1") %>%
  set_capacity("type1", 0) %>%
  join(main) %>%
  release("type1")

type2 <- trajectory() %>%
  ...

type3 <- trajectory() %>%
  ...

Instead of "round-robin", you can provide your own R function to
implement any policy you want. There's a quite sophisticated example
of this pattern in the following vignette:

https://r-simmer.org/articles/simmer-aa-5g#mobile-traffic-backhauling-with-fttx

--
Iñaki Úcar

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I am new to simmer but highly interested. I need to devise a simulation where one specific is that we can only generate new arrivals if a buffer is not empty. The state of the buffer depends on the previous execution of the process - i.e. we start with a full buffer, some steps deplete it some fill it up. At a given moment I want to strt a new trajectory, but only if there is at least one element in the buffer. Can this be done in simmer?

Thanks a lot for any help!!!
Kind regards

At a given moment I want to strt a new trajectory, but only if there is at least one element in the buffer. Can this be done in simmer?

There may be several ways depending on your specific needs. You can
set a global attribute (see ?add_global) and a generator that depends
on that variable (i.e., that spits out arrivals depending on the
reading of such a variable, see ?get_global). But you can also read
the status of resources (see ?get_capacity and subsequent functions in
the same help page). Another more sophisticated and more flexible
mechanism would be to set up a control trajectory with a single
arrival in a loop (see ?rollback). There, you can call activities that
apply a finer control over generators (see ?activate, ?set_source).

Iñaki

messages.body_plain:
I think I figured out a solution, what do you think of this ?

I have two types of resources "consumers" who reduce the buffer and "producers" who increase the buffer, both always by 1 unit.
I would define 3 global attributes, BufferSize, NextTake and NextAdd.

The BufferSize woud keep track of the size of the buffer.
NextTake is the time the consumer will finish its present job and will be able to process the next one.
NextAdd is the time the producer will finish its job and will be able to add the unit to the buffer.

The generator would look at the buffer. If it is empty it would return the time stored in NextAdd . That means that the consumer will need to wait until the next unit becomes available.
If the buffer is not empty then the generator wil return the time stored in NextTake , that is the unit will be released the moment the consumer becomes free.

The consumer always reduces the buffer by 1 when it starts and the producesr always increases the buffer by 1 when it ends.

Thanks a lot for your help!
